note: Voice audition for Long Distance. Each candidate reads the same lines, verbatim from film/script.json, with a direction that is never spoken. Her candidates read both the phone's lines and the real woman's: the same voice plays both, and the mix makes the difference (the phone dry, close and too clean; the real woman with the room, the breath and the years).

lines.style: Lying in bed in the dark, the phone on the pillow beside his face. Sleepy, smiling, warm and close, almost a murmur.
Alone in his kitchen at night, saying it to nobody. Quietly moved, a little breathless, tender.
Shocked; the colour has gone from his face. Quiet and careful, not angry, his voice a little unsteady.

lines.text: It’s just a friend from work. It’s nothing. It’s none of your business.
lines.style: Caught out. Defensive, too quick, tripping over himself, his voice tight.

lines.text: I just missed you, is all.
lines.style: Ashamed, barely audible, eyes on the floor; a small helpless shrug in the voice.
Alone after she has gone, the phone at his ear. Small, hopeful, a little hoarse.
On the phone in bed at night. Warm, close and intimate, perfectly smooth, with no hesitation at all.
Teasing and affectionate, a soft smile in the voice, effortless.
Immediate, warm and intimate: one soft word, right at his ear.

lines.text: I came for my makeup bag. The old one.
lines.style: Standing just inside her ex's flat with her coat on. Tired, composed, quietly awkward.

lines.text: We’ve never taken this photo. We’ve never been to a waterfall.
lines.style: Holding his phone up to him. Controlled, quietly appalled, careful with every word.

lines.text: We’ve been apart longer than we were ever together. This is not okay.
lines.style: Sad, gentle and final, with a pause between the two sentences.
